catalog_quote: 31. O accento colloca-se em regra geral sobre a penúltima syllaba de cada palavra tetense. Ex.: múnfu, pessoa; muâna, filho; muamúna, homem; wakâzi, mulheres; múi, aldeia; karúma, calor; nyôka, cobra; korokôro, bagre; kufamanga, correr; kuremekêza, respeitar; kufúna, querer; kukumbuka, lembrar-se. 32. Observação. — Em geral, não escrevemos o accento, excepto em alguns casos em que poderia offerecer-se duvida seria, como kúsua, quebrar; kusúa, ter saudades, descascar mantimento, etc. 33. Nas formas dos verbos terminados em ua, ya, a syllaba accentuada é a penúltima. Ex.: kubâdua, nascer; kúmua, beber; kup'êdua, ser morto; kusâmua, gingar; kúgua, cair; kúdya, comer; kumênya, bater; kup'ônya, falhar. Exceptuam-se kusúa, descascar; kufeúa, kttkúwa, gritar; kusíya, deixar, e alguns outros verbos. ... 35. Os verbos passivos iwa, idua, ara, edua, tomam accento na penúltima. ... 37. As partícul…

audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding passage (Courtois 1900, Cap. III § 2.º 'Do accento', nos. 31-38, pp. 9-10) is present verbatim in the held archive.org djvu text at lines 1162-1249, page break and index entry confirming pp. 9-10. The source is a 1900 Jesuit missionary grammar — old and pedagogical, hence 'thin' rather than 'well-sourced' — but it is explicit, rule-plus-exceptions, and nothing found contradicts it: Hyman's 2017/2019 Bantu tone overview (fetched sources, p. 162) classes Nyungwe N43 among the handful of non-tonal Bantu languages (with Sena, Tumbuka, Swahili), which fits a fixed-penult stress coding; the SIL 2013 grammar notes (fetched sources via Wayback, 44 pp.) are silent on prosody; the held Langa da Câmara 2018 syntax article is silent. No phonology article, instrumental study or dissertation on Nyungwe prosody was found in Glottolog's 10 descriptive refs or on the web before the search budge

sources.citation: Hyman, Larry M. 2017. Bantu Tone Overview. UC Berkeley PhonLab Annual Report 13: 162-177 (pre-print of the chapter in Van de Velde et al. eds. 2019, The Bantu Languages, 2nd ed. / Oxford Guide).
sources.quote: 'Most of the ca. 500 Bantu languages have at least a binary tonal contrast realized as surface H(igh) vs. L(ow). The relatively few exceptions include a discontinous band of languages starting in Mozambique with Sena [N44] and Nyungwe [N43], up around Lake Nyasa to Tumbuka [N21] and Nyakyusa [M31] ... and finally the best known case, Swahili (G42).' No statement on stress position.
